A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPME research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of test calibration and power, counterfactual sampling, computational runtime, and recommendation-policy evaluation in Section 6 and Appendix 14.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Warfarin and dSprites evaluations, together with additional runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The plug-in and doubly robust estimators, DR-KPT procedure, kernel herding, and discrete/continuous-action algorithms are retained. New kernel configurations and benchmark applications do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds semi-synthetic Warfarin dosage evaluation using patient covariates and clinical cost outcomes, plus dSprites evaluation with 64×64 image outcomes and two-dimensional actions. These substantially extend the earlier synthetic scalar/binary-outcome coverage; the earlier experiments remain.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates a polynomial-kernel KPT comparator alongside the existing RBF and linear variants, including in the added synthetic runtime comparison. KPT-linear matches the earlier PT-linear comparator. The recommendation-experiment baselines are retained.

E3.justification: Appendices 14.1.4–14.1.5 introduce benchmark-specific protocols, including Warfarin filtering and dose-tolerance costs, image-vector kernel evaluation, 3,000 dSprites samples, weight clipping at 100,000, and fixed DR regularization of 100. Timing evaluations also extend to larger sample sizes. These are added protocols, not established reruns or replacements of the original experiments.

E4.justification: New Tables 7–8 extend computational scaling analysis to larger samples and additional kernel variants. The sample-splitting ablation in Figure 4 and recommendation sensitivity analyses in Figure 6 are unchanged; the new benchmark accuracy tables are not themselves new ablations.

E5.justification: The original repeated-run counts and confidence-interval practices remain. The added Warfarin and dSprites protocols specify 100 seeds, but their rejection-rate Tables 1–2 report point estimates without confidence intervals, unlike the earlier testing plots. No increase in repetitions for existing experiments is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark and runtime results. For dSprites Scenario IV, Table 2 reports 0.656 rejection for DR-KPT-rbf versus 0.054 for KPT-rbf. Warfarin Scenario III reports 0.99 for DR-KPT-rbf versus 1.00 for KPT-linear, so superiority is not universal. Earlier plotted results and corresponding runtime and sampling table values are retained.

T1.justification: Equation (13) and its accompanying beta definition correct the mixture of estimated and population conditional embeddings, restoring a population test-function definition. The proofs and convergence rates otherwise remain. The non-degeneracy condition newly displayed in the main Theorem 7 already appeared in v1 Appendix 12.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the assertion of improved uniform convergence rates, retaining the narrower claim of improved convergence rates. The central CPME, plug-in estimation, doubly robust estimation, testing, and sampling contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies CPME as an interventional, second-rung causal quantity and explains why stochastic interventions support continuous-treatment influence functions without localization. The discussion shifts future directions toward MMD gradient flows and weaker identification assumptions.

D1.justification: The new experimental appendices provide substantial reproduction information: clinical inclusion criteria and covariates, outcome construction, propensity fitting, image generation and flattening, clipping, and regularization. The repository link and hardware information already existed in v1. Some dSprites details remain inconsistent between the main text and appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning sequential evaluation, continuous-treatment estimation, the new datasets, and MMD gradient flows. It sharpens the distinction from earlier treatment-effect methods while retaining the original positioning around counterfactual embeddings and Hilbert-valued influence functions.

P1.justification: v2 refines terminology, expands the influence-function explanation, separates testing and sampling into numbered experimental subsections, and rewrites the discussion. It also adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The principal section sequence and theoretical appendix organization remain.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS template changes typography, text width, title and author presentation, and display placement throughout. Four tables are added. All six figures retain their original plots, although their placement and sizing change; Figure 1's caption corrects 'power' to 'false positive rate.'

improvement.justification: Warfarin and dSprites provide useful empirical support beyond v1's synthetic scalar/binary examples, accompanied by detailed protocols and broader runtime analysis. However, the main text calls the dSprites alternative a shifted mixture while its appendix describes an intercept shift, and the new rejection-rate tables omit confidence intervals. These reporting limitations temper the gains; the core methods and theoretical results are essentially retained.
